properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 29 at 8:32AM MST until September 29 at 2:30PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
FFWTWC

The National Weather Service in Tucson has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
North Central Pima County in southeastern Arizona...
Pinal County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 230 PM MST.

* At 832 AM MST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Up to 1.5 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are possible
in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Marana, Sells, Eloy, Avra Valley, Kearny, Dudleyville, Santa Rosa,
Picacho, San Isidro, Picacho Peak State Park, Pinal Airpark,
Picture Rocks, Red Rock, Cactus Forest, Covered Wells, Anegam, Gu
Oidak, Palo Verde Stand, Ak Chin and Queens Well.

This includes the following highways...
Route 79 between mile markers 95 and 128. Route 86 between mile
markers 89 and 112. Route 87 between mile markers 116 and 124. Route
77 between mile markers 122 and 134. Route 177 between mile markers
139 and 158. Interstate 10 between mile markers 205 and 242.

This includes the following Flash Flood Prone Locations...
Suizo Rd at Cadillac Wash, Sunland Gin Rd at Greene Wash, Sasco Rd at
Santa Cruz Wash, Park Link Dr between I-10 and HWY 79, Twin Peaks Rd
between Sanders and Sandario and Sil Nakya Wash at Route 34.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Massachusetts...

Taunton River Near Bridgewater affecting Plymouth and Bristol
Counties.

For the Taunton River...including Bridgewater...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Taunton River near Bridgewater.

* WHEN...Until late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Backwater flooding from the Taunton River
will cause flooding of lower Purchade Brook in Middleboro.  This
will cause Woloski Park to become impassable by most vehicles for
an extended period of time.  Beware of the dangers of crossing
flooded roadways. The water may be deeper than you think.
Floodwaters have the ability to damage roadways. Heed the advice of
local officials, and evacuate if asked to do so.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:45 AM EDT Tuesday the stage was 9.1 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:45 AM EDT Tuesday was 9.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
tomorrow evening and continue falling to 6.4 feet Friday morning.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
SMWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL from 20 to 60 NM
excluding the territorial waters of Bahamas...

* Until 1245 PM EDT.

* At 1201 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 37 nm east of Pacific Reef, moving
southeast at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* The severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or the National Weather
Service. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on Facebook
and Twitter.

Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Tuesday the stage was 2.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Tuesday was 2.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 2.6 feet today, and then gradually subside through Minor
Flood Stage this week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 2.6
feet on 10/14/1996.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EDT.

SMWTBW

The National Weather Service in Ruskin has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Bonita Beach to Englewood FL out 20 NM...
Waters from Bonita Beach to Englewood FL out 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 1230 PM EDT.

* At 1147 AM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 27 nm west of North Captiva Island, moving
east at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats, damage
vessels, and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots,
suddenly higher waves, frequent lightning, and heavy
downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* The severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 29 at 8:51AM MDT until September 29 at 11:45AM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
FFWEPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
South Central Grant County in southwestern New Mexico...
East Central Hidalgo County in southwestern New Mexico...
Southwestern Luna County in southwestern New Mexico...

* Until 1145 AM MDT.

* At 851 AM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.75 and 1.25 inches of
rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Hachita and Hachita Valley.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
